thread:
maria: Quick check — landed a small change to the routing sidecar that adds a per-tenant affinity gating step based on cost delta. It's gated behind a feature flag. Thoughts on the runtime surface?
jonathan: Nice. Do we expose this as a policy predicate (eval-only) or as an admission gate that can block requests?
maria: Admission gate for the initial roll — simpler and gives deterministic fallbacks. We'll keep an eval-only variant later.
kevin: Concern: any admission path that runs synchronously can increase p99. Did you measure impact on batching?
eva: ran a microbench with 128 qps and typical seq len. Median adds ~0.9ms; p99 ~2.5ms in worst case (GC in sidecar). Continuous batching saw ~1% throughput reduction at target load.
sanjay: Could we implement a fast-path predicate: short-circuit accept for cost_delta < 0.05 or region_penalty < 0.1, otherwise defer to async scoring? That keeps common case very cheap.
shanice: +1 to a fast path. Also worried about oscillation if region_penalty flips frequently — need hysteresis or smoothing.
maria: Agreed. Proposed plan: (1) sync fast-path predicate (cheap checks), (2) async heavier scorer for borderline cases with sampled re-eval to update cache, (3) exponential smoothing on region_penalty. I'll put this in the RFC.
jonathan: Also add an invariant: decisions must be deterministic for the same inputs (no non-deterministic randomness). Otherwise A/B and rollout comparisons become noisy.
kevin: Telemetry: tag every request with decision_reason and gate_version to enable per-tenant debugging and rollbacks.
eva: I'll add histograms: decision_latency_ms, fast_path_rate, async_resolution_time, and cache_hit_ratio.
sanjay: Implementation note: avoid blocking the inference thread. Do scoring in the sidecar event loop and keep a small LRU cache for recent tenant decisions keyed by (tenant, region, model_variant).
shanice: For rollout controls we should support percent-based opt-ins and manual tenant whitelists via control-plane flags.
maria: Draft interface I'm thinking of: 
```
PolicyAdmission.evaluateSync(signals) -> { decision: "accept" | "fallback" | "defer", reason: string, gate_version: string }
PolicyAdmission.evaluateAsync(signals) -> { score: number, confidence: number }
```
Backward compatible: if evaluateSync returns "defer", runtime will consult cached async score if available or fallback to tier routing.
jonathan: Make sure evaluateSync is lightweight: no allocations for common path, avoid heap; use pre-sized buffers.
kevin: Perf test checklist: microbench at 50/200/500 qps, batch sizes 1/8/16, p50/p95/p99 for decision latency and end-to-end token latency. Also test cold cache vs warm cache.
maria: I'll produce the RFC + perf numbers. Action items: RFC by Tue (maria), perf microbench (eva + kevin), telemetry dashboard prototype (eva), control-plane rollout knobs (sanjay).
ops-bot: deploy: routing-sidecar v2.3.canary started (flag: affinity-gating).
shanice: Danger scenario to document in the RFC: "small oscillation -> herd migration" where many tenants flip fallback at once causing capacity churn. Propose global dampening knob.
sanjay: Add sampled logs of decision transitions so we can reconstruct sequences that caused churn.
maria: Great — will include. Any objections to the hybrid sync/async surface?
jonathan: No objections. :thumbsup:
kevin: No objections. We should keep rollout conservative.
maria: Thanks team — will draft and ping for review.
